name: MAI Code 2
archDisplay: Decoder-only transformer with sparse Mixture-of-Experts layers and an integrated vision encoder; 1.05M-token context (922K input, 128K output); reasoning effort low to max
note: Microsoft AI's MAI Code 2, released Nov 17, 2026 (model card) in GitHub Copilot, billed per token under usage-based billing. Microsoft's larger agentic coding model for complex, long-horizon software engineering, available on Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise. Parameters are left null because the card contradicts itself: its summary says '50B-100B (80B active)' while Section 1 says 77B active and about 2.8T total. Price is GitHub's promotional rate ($0.5/$2.5 per Mtok) until May 17, 2027, then $1/$5, following the Gemini 4 Carbon precedent of filing the current introductory headline price. Weights are not distributed (model card). Predecessor is null: the card compares the family with MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, which is not in this corpus and is a different family. Rows come from the model card's quality table (Section 3: MSBench with the GitHub Copilot CLI harness, subagents off, max reasoning, pass rate) plus GPQA from its CBRN evaluation table (settings not stated). NOT FILED: SWE Atlas 43.1 (the full three-workflow benchmark, not the Codebase QnA column); the card's advanced-autonomy table gives different DeepSWE 1.1 (60.2) and SWE Atlas (80.9) figures and GAIA 67.27, and its loss-of-control table gives Terminal-Bench 4 26.3, all under unstated settings, so they are left out; the launch post's comparisons are relative only. Not on Vals AI yet.
